title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Quiet weekend, no new session — Friday's close still stands. Nasdaq fell 0.9%, S&P 500 fell 0.4%, Dow rose 0.1%, as AI-trade jitters build ahead of Nvidia's Tuesday earnings; Nvidia itself closed down 2%.

Markets: Treasury yields eased Friday after Thursday's sharp rise on hardening Fed rate-hike bets (10-year near 5.15%); oil ticked up on Mideast conflict risk, while IEA sees the global oil market tipping back into surplus this quarter as Gulf exports recover to 82% of pre-war levels.

Companies: Nvidia's board named CFO Colette Kress interim CEO and director Harvey Jones its first-ever board chair after Jensen Huang resigned amid reports of affairs and an alleged tie to a suspected Chinese spy; a permanent-successor search is underway.

Companies: Anthropic, maker of Claude, is still targeting a roughly $1.33T IPO valuation, with shares expected to begin trading Thursday; CEO Dario Amodei says he hopes to 'underpromise and overdeliver.'
Companies: Microsoft shares recovered from a widespread Teams/Outlook outage; chipmaker Cerebras beat Q3 revenue estimates, raised its forecast, and announced a new Microsoft deal.
Macro/Policy: October wholesale prices (PPI) rose 0.3% m/m but the 12-month rate climbed to a hot 6.5% from 6.3%, reinforcing a hawkish Fed tilt ahead of Wednesday's FOMC minutes.

Macro/Policy: Commerce Secretary Lutnick faces bipartisan Congressional pressure (Sens. Warren, Kennedy) over delayed chip-export-control action tied to the Huang scandal, though the White House continues to back him.
